warnings.title: BEFORE YOU REPORT A 'SUDDEN' HARDWARE FAILURE...
bullets: DO NOT GIVE YOUR LAPTOP A DRINK (It is NOT thirsty).
DO NOT USE IT ON A DUVET OR HEATING PAD (It is NOT a pet).
REMEMBER: We can literally smell the caramel macchiato.
Note: Constant nagging about these issues will result in 'The Slow Queue'.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU EXPLAIN HOW YOUR FILE 'JUST DISAPPEARED'...
bullets: Do not delete files from your desktop to 'clean up'.
We can see your browser history (including that recipe site).
Yes, we check the recycle bin. It's often right there.
Note: Claiming data loss due to 'ghosts' will result in our 'Spiritual Audit' procedure.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU CLAIM YOUR PC 'HAS A VIRUS' OR 'NOTHING CHANGED'...
bullets: "Nothing changed" is a lie forged in the first furnace of humanity. We can see the registry cleaners and coupon plugins.
Your PC boots slower than continental drift because you have six expired antiviruses fighting for dominance.
Task Manager is unresponsive because your CPU is currently having religious visions.
Note: Having Norton, McAfee, and Avast running simultaneously does not make you secure; it makes your hard drive a warzone.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU DECLARE A FULL-SCALE 'CYBERATTACK'...
bullets: Your ex is not "hacking into the mainframe" to rearrange your desktop icons. You dragged them by accident while violently scrolling.
That terrifying pop-up screaming that you have 500 critically infected files is just a Chrome notification you explicitly allowed from a sketchy recipe website.
Closing the browser tab fixes 99% of your "hacker" problems.
Note: Willful ignorance is not a computer virus, but it certainly spreads like one.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU LOOK ME IN THE EYE AND SAY 'IT WAS LIKE THAT WHEN I OPENED IT'...
bullets: Physics is a real, measurable constant. Laptop screens do not spontaneously shatter from the center outward due to "air pressure." You closed it with a pen on the keyboard.
Motherboards do not naturally grow sticky, caffeinated, brown crystals in the wild.
Lying doesn't protect you; it just guarantees the diagnostic process takes twice as long. We charge by the hour.
Note: We have seen it all. We have fixed it all. Your clumsy attempt at deception is deeply insulting to our intelligence.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU COMPLAIN THAT 'THE SERVER IS DOWN'...
bullets: The Docker containers are running perfectly fine.
The network routing is optimal.
Your inability to connect to the shared drive is because you accidentally joined the 'Guest' Wi-Fi. Again.
Note: Blaming the core infrastructure for your forgotten VPN login is a punishable offense.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU SUBMIT A TICKET LABELED 'URGENT: EVERYTHING IS BROKEN'...
bullets: "It doesn't work" is not a symptom; it is an emotional state.
We cannot troubleshoot the error message you immediately clicked "OK" on without reading.
"ASAP" is not a timeline; it is a manifestation of your anxiety.
Note: Tickets consisting of a single vague sentence will be routed directly to /dev/null.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU ARGUE WITH THE DIAGNOSIS...
bullets: You brought this to me because you couldn't fix it. Do not suddenly start arguing with the person who actually can.
If your "IT buddy" actually knew how to fix it, it wouldn't be sitting on my workbench right now.
"But I read an article that said..." is the fastest way to get your machine shoved to the absolute back of the repair queue.
Note: Unsolicited technical advice from the person who just locked themselves out of their own email will be ignored.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU SAY 'I COULD HAVE DONE THAT MYSELF'...
bullets: Then why didn't you?
Yes, the final fix was running a single PowerShell command. The job was knowing which of the 10,000 commands wouldn't vaporize the active directory.
You are not paying for the five minutes it took to type the script; you are paying for the years of suffering it took to know why we type the script.
Note: If you attempt to "do it yourself" next time and fail, your ticket will be placed at the bottom of a very deep, dark queue.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU CLAIM YOU 'ALREADY REBOOTED'...
bullets: Turning your monitor off and back on is not a system reboot.
Logging out and logging back in is not a reboot.
Closing the laptop lid is definitely not a reboot.
Task Manager shows an uptime of 47 days, 14 hours, and 12 minutes. The machine remembers. We can see the truth.
Note: Lying to your IT tech about rebooting adds an automatic 24-hour 'Observation Period' to your ticket.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU YELL AT YOUR DEVICE TO 'JUST FIX ITSELF'...
bullets: Your computer is not a sentient being. The AI does not literally "hear" your voice; it is receiving processed text from a microphone array.
Screaming louder and slower at your webcam will not magically resolve a corrupted driver.
Threatening to throw the machine out the window does not intimidate the silicon. It just makes the people in the cubicles next to you uncomfortable.
Note: If you physically strike the hardware in frustration, your warranty is instantly vaporized, and my hourly rate doubles.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU TELL ME 'COMPUTERS JUST HATE ME'...
bullets: Technology does not have the emotional capacity to hate you. It responds exclusively to binary logic, electrical currents, and the commands you physically input.
If every single machine you touch inexplicably breaks, the common denominator is not a digital curse. The common denominator is you.
Treating a high-performance machine like a cutting board, a coaster, or a space heater and then acting like a victim when it dies is peak human delusion.
Note: A machine cannot hate you, but the IT guy fixing it definitely can.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU GIVE YOUR LAPTOP A DRINK...
bullets: Your laptop is not thirsty. It does not want your coffee, your tea, your water, or your caramel macchiato.
We can smell the sticky residue. We will find the corroded motherboard traces. We will know exactly what you did.
"It just stopped working" is not a valid description when the insides look like a crime scene from a CSI episode.
Note: The diagnostic fee remains the same whether you admit to the spill or force us to find the evidence ourselves.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU TRY TO INVENT A 'NEW' EXCUSE FOR THE DAMAGE...
bullets: I have been doing this for over a decade. I promise you, I have seen every conceivable way a human being can destroy a motherboard.
Your "unprecedented" hardware failure is a textbook liquid spill.
Please save us both the theatrical performance.
Note: Lying about how it broke means I have to spend extra time acting surprised when I find out exactly how you broke it. You will be billed for my acting.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BLAME 'DIVINE INTERVENTION' FOR PHYSICAL DAMAGE...
bullets: Lightning striking the local substation and frying your ungrounded motherboard because you refused to buy a R200 surge protector is not a mysterious Act of God. It is a highly predictable Act of Stupidity.
Deities do not randomly descend from the heavens to shatter the LCD screen of your tablet from the center outward. You dropped it in the driveway.
Blaming a higher power for your refusal to safely eject a USB drive before yanking it out is theological malpractice.
If you bring me a laptop that looks like it was run over by a bakkie and claim "divine intervention," I am going to charge you an exorcism fee.
Note: Holy water immediately and permanently voids the manufacturer's warranty. Do not sprinkle things on the motherboard.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BRING IN A DEVICE WITH 'VITALLY IMPORTANT FILES'...
bullets: If the files were truly important, they would exist in more than one physical location.
Handing me a clicking, smoking hard drive and saying, "My entire business is on there, don't lose it," is not a backup strategy. It is a tragedy.
I am an IT Technician. I do not have a sterile data-recovery cleanroom in my back pocket.
Note: Presenting you with a quote for R15,000 professional platter-recovery services usually cures your sudden attachment to those "important files" immediately.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BLAME 'EVER SINCE YOU FIXED MY PRINTER'...
bullets: Fixing your paper jam last Tuesday did not cause your motherboard to short-circuit today.
Installing an antivirus does not make you forget your online banking password.
Causation does not equal correlation, especially when your timeline involves you dropping the machine on a tile floor in the interim.
Note: The "Ever Since" warranty only covers the space-time continuum directly related to the original repair, not your subsequent poor life choices.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU DEMAND SUPPORT FOR YOUR 'BARGAIN' HARDWARE...
bullets: Buying the absolute cheapest, no-name tablet or knock-off accessory online does not make you a financial genius; it makes you my problem.
There are no drivers. There is no manual. The manufacturer's website is a parked domain from 2015.
No, I cannot "just write a script to make it work." I am an IT Technician, not a necromancer.
Note: If the device feels suspiciously hollow and rattles when you shake it, do not bring it to this desk.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BRING IN MYSTERY PARTS YOU BOUGHT ON CLEARANCE...
bullets: We provide professional IT services, we are not a Lego assembly service for the cheapest knock-off components you managed to find scrolling Takealot at 2 AM.
If you bring me an unbranded motherboard, RAM that smells like ozone, and a power supply held together by sheer hope, I will not guarantee it will boot.
"Can't you just make it fit?" is a question for a carpenter.
Note: Providing your own sketchy hardware doubles the diagnostic fee and completely voids any sympathy when the machine inevitably catches fire.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BRING IN THAT 'AMAZING DEAL' YOU BOUGHT ON SALE...
bullets: That absolute bottom-tier laptop you grabbed off Takealot or Incredible Connection for next to nothing is basically a glorified digital photo frame with a keyboard.
You cannot run heavy accounting software, render 4K video, or host your local databases on a Celeron processor with eMMC storage.
No, I cannot "just make it faster." You bought a toaster, and now you are mad it cannot fly.
Note: I cannot download more RAM for you. Please accept the consequences of your financial decisions.

title: Power, Shutdown & The Overheating Backpack Saga
description: Power, Shutdown & The Overheating Backpack Saga

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU SHOVE THAT LAPTOP INTO YOUR OVERSTUFFED BACKPACK...
bullets: "The screen went black" does NOT mean "Powered Off."
Those little flashing lights on the side? They are desperately trying to finish a Windows update. Give them 10 seconds before snapping the lid shut.
Your backpack is highly insulated. Zipping a running laptop into it creates a portable, high-budget sauna.
Note: Claiming your laptop "just started making jet engine noises" after marinating in its own heat for two hours will result in your ticket being reclassified as 'Arson'.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU CLAIM THE POWER LIGHTS ARE 'A HOAX'...
bullets: "The screen went black" does NOT mean "Powered Off."
Those little flashing lights on the side? They are desperately trying to finish a Windows update. Give them 10 seconds before snapping the lid shut.
Your backpack is highly insulated. Zipping a running laptop into it creates a portable, high-budget sauna.
Note: Repeated overheating reports due to this action will result in a ticket reclassification: 'The Arson Incident'.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU HOLD THE POWER BUTTON DURING A WINDOWS UPDATE...
bullets: "Getting Windows ready" requires patience, not physical violence.
Interrupting it guarantees the next 4 hours will be spent undoing changes, failing repairs, and collecting sadness.
Your Event Viewer now has 14,372 warnings that read like cursed poetry.
Note: Force-quitting an update does not make it go away; it just makes it angry.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU COMPLAIN THAT YOUR BRAND NEW LAPTOP IS 'TOO SLOW'...
bullets: People think "SSD" means fast. No. It just means the suffering loads quicker.
8GB of RAM shared with integrated graphics running 47 preinstalled "help" utilities is a crime, not a feature.
Idle RAM usage is at 82% because of your OEM bloatware kingdom.
Note: A machine that costs less than a decent office chair will perform exactly as expected.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BLAME ME FOR THE SERVER REBOOTING...
bullets: We live in South Africa. If you didn't save your work before the scheduled loadshedding block hit, that is a matter strictly between you, Eskom, and whatever deity you pray to.
The UPS is designed to give you exactly enough time to click "Save" and safely shut down the system. It is not designed to let you finish your GTA Online heist.
No, I cannot "tweak the settings to make the battery last longer."
Note: Expecting infinite power from a lead-acid battery during a Stage 4 outage will result in your immediate transfer to the 'Thoughts and Prayers' queue.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU USE IT ON A DUVET OR HEATING PAD...
bullets: Your laptop is not a pet. It does not need to be warm and cozy.
Blocking every single ventilation intake with soft fabric is the fastest way to thermally throttle your CPU into an early grave.
That "thermal event" we warned you about? That's what just happened.
Note: We can tell by the melted dust bunnies in your heat sink exactly what surface you've been using it on.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU EXPLAIN HOW YOUR PASSWORD 'WAS JUST WORKING YESTERDAY'...
bullets: Your "complex" password is not "P@$$w0rd!".
Yes, caps lock counts. No, we cannot "just disable it."
Your memory of changing it last week is not evidence.
Note: Repeated attempts using "password123" will result in a mandatory security lecture (with PowerPoint).

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU ASK WHY GOOGLE 'DOESN'T KNOW IT'S YOU'...
bullets: You changed your phone, your number, your recovery email, and your location.
To the automated security system, you look exactly like a cybercriminal wearing your own skin.
"I forgot my password" does not exempt you from basic account recovery setup.
Note: We cannot magically bypass corporate security protocols just because you are "in a hurry."

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU ASK ME TO 'BYPASS THE OTP'...
bullets: The One-Time PIN is literally the only thing standing between your life savings and a teenager with a laptop on the other side of the world.
No, I cannot "turn it off because it's annoying."

If your phone number changed and you didn't tell the bank, and now you can't receive the SMS to authorize your payment, that is a 'You' problem. I cannot hack the cellular tower to reroute your messages.
Note: Any request to intentionally bypass two-factor authentication on a financial platform will be met with uproarious, mocking laughter until you leave the premises.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU ASK ME TO 'JUST OPEN YOUR GOOGLE DOCS' TO FIX A TYPO...
bullets: I am an IT Technician, not an omnipotent digital deity. I do not have native, backdoor access to your private Google account.
I cannot bypass your two-factor authentication, and I cannot "just peek" at your documents without your active session and credentials.
Stop assuming I am sitting at my desk reading your private files. I have an entire homelab of Docker containers to maintain; your data is not that interesting.
Note: If you refuse to type in your own password during a remote session because "I should already have it," your ticket is instantly closed.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BLAME THE 'BANKING APP UPDATE' FOR YOUR EMPTY ACCOUNT...
bullets: Software updates patch security vulnerabilities and add features; they do not steal your money.

If your account is empty, it is because you clicked a link in an SMS that said "URGENT: YOUR PARCEL IS DELAYED" and gleefully typed your credit card details into a website hosted in a basement three continents away.
Uninstalling and reinstalling the banking app will not magically reverse a wire transfer.
Note: Telling me "but the website looked so real" does not change the fact that the URL was www.fnb-secure-login-totally-real-update.biz.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU SEND AN URGENT TICKET ABOUT THE INTERNET BEING 'DOWN'...
bullets: Check your cables, especially the power one.
"Off and On" is not a suggestion, it's a diagnosis.
Your local router is not our network's responsibility.
Note: Failure to check the power plug will double your wait time.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU TRY TO 'TWEAK' THE NETWORK TO MAKE IT FASTER...
bullets: A Mikrotik router is not a toy. If you do not know the difference between a subnet mask and a MAC address, step away from the blinking lights.

Hitting the recessed "Reset" button with a paperclip because your Spotify wouldn't load did not "refresh the connection." It wiped a heavily customized configuration and brought the entire business to a standstill.
We know exactly what time you decided to play Systems Administrator. The firewall logs do not lie.
Note: Unplugging the main switch to charge your vape is grounds for immediate and permanent exile.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU SUBMIT A TICKET SAYING THE PRINTER 'SUDDENLY STOPPED'...
bullets: Printers do not break; they negotiate terms.
A status of "Ready" is a bold-faced lie. It is actually just evaluating its next victim.
Printing successfully from your phone does not mean it is fixed.
Note: Staring at the machine is not a troubleshooting step; it is a loyalty exam.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU TELL ME 'THE PRINTER TOLD ME TO CHANGE THE TONER'...
bullets: Printers are notorious liars with a vested interest in selling you more plastic cylinders of expensive dust.
"Low Toner" actually means "you can probably get another 400 pages out of this if you take the cartridge out and give it a good shake."
If you replace the cartridge the literal second the warning pops up, you are throwing away company money.
Note: Anyone caught replacing a toner cartridge that still has weight to it will be forced to manually transcribe their documents with a ballpoint pen.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BLAME THE 'VPN' FOR YOUR INABILITY TO WORK...
bullets: My Tailscale configuration is routing perfectly. The network is stable, secure, and fully operational.
The reason you cannot reach the company server is because you are trying to work from a coffee shop whose public Wi-Fi actively blocks everything except web browsing.
A secure tunnel cannot physically push data through a firewall built by a barista.
Note: Submitting a high-priority ticket because your favorite café has bad internet is an abuse of the support desk. Buy a better data plan.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU TRY TO 'UPGRADE' THE OFFICE HARDWARE...
bullets: RAM is slotted. CPUs are gently socketed. If you have to push down so hard that the motherboard visibly bends, you are committing a hardware felony.
Splicing random wires into the power supply because you watched a tutorial on custom ARGB LED strips is how you burn down the accounting department.
A cheap soldering iron and blind confidence are the most terrifying combination known to IT.
Note: We can literally smell the burnt silicon from down the hall. Your workstation is now a crime scene.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU SUBMIT A REQUEST TO 'INSTALL MICROSOFT'...
bullets: "Microsoft" is a multi-billion dollar corporation, not an application.
If you mean 'Word', please say 'Word'.
We cannot read your mind to determine if you need Windows, Teams, Edge, or OneDrive.
Note: Vague software requests will be met with the mandatory installation of the ancient Visual C++ runtime necromancy pack.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU TELL US YOU 'OPTIMIZED' YOUR OWN REGISTRY...
bullets: Running a free "speed booster" you found on page 4 of Google does not make your PC faster. It makes your OS a crime scene.
Your game booster isn't freeing up RAM; it's mining crypto and sending your keystrokes to a server in another time zone.

I am not going to painstakingly untangle the digital knot you tied. I am going to nuke the drive from orbit and run a proper system optimizer script to rebuild it from scratch. Your custom cursors and desktop widgets are gone forever.
Note: "Speeding up" your machine via TikTok tutorials completely voids your right to complain about the resulting blue screens.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU USE A 'REGISTRY CLEANER' TO FIX AN AUDIO ISSUE...
bullets: You did not fix the audio; you lobotomized the operating system.
I am not going to painstakingly reverse-engineer the 4,000 critical system files your "free tool" just deleted.
I am going to launch my custom PowerShell system optimizer, wipe the drive, and rebuild the machine from scratch.
Note: Yes, all of the heavily encrypted, unsaved Word documents you kept exclusively in the Recycle Bin are gone forever. The script has no mercy, and neither do I.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU DEPLOY YOUR 'QUICK FIX' TO THE ENVIRONMENT...
bullets: "It works on my machine" means absolutely nothing when your machine is a chaotic wasteland held together by duct tape and disabled firewalls.
Blindly spinning up a Docker container you found on a random GitHub repo with zero understanding of the required permission management is exactly how everything breaks.
You are not "innovating," you are creating a massive security vulnerability that I now have to clean up.
Note: Root access is a privilege, not a birthright, and yours is hereby revoked.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU COMPLAIN THAT THE 'NEW SOFTWARE IS TOO COMPLICATED'...
bullets: Your refusal to read a three-step instruction manual is not a software bug.
Clicking every single button on the screen as fast as you can until something happens is not a troubleshooting methodology; it is how toddlers play with iPads.
I wrote that custom script specifically to automate your workflow. If you delete the shortcut because "it looked weird," you are back to doing it manually.
Note: "I am not a computer person" is no longer a valid excuse in the 21st century. It is just an admission of defeat.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU DEMAND THAT I INSTALL WINDOWS 11 ON YOUR DECADE-OLD LAPTOP...
bullets: Your machine was built during a time when 4GB of RAM was considered a luxury. It does not meet the minimum requirements, the recommended requirements, or the spiritual requirements to run a modern OS.
I can deploy a lightweight Linux ISO from my local mirrors to make it usable as a web browsing machine.
If you absolutely insist on forcing Windows onto it, be prepared to measure boot times with a calendar instead of a stopwatch.
Note: I am a technician, not an alchemist. I cannot turn your 2012 e-waste into a high-end workstation.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU COMPLAIN ABOUT MY POWERSHELL SCRIPTS...
bullets: Yes, I ran the system_optimizer on your machine. Yes, it removed your 14 malicious browser toolbars and your desktop bloatware.
If you manually interrupt my Python scripts because you "didn't know what that black window was doing," you are officially banned from the local repository.
My automation workflows do not "break" your machine; they enforce a baseline of digital hygiene you were previously incapable of maintaining.
Note: If you delete my n8n webhooks because you think they are "viruses," I will replace your office chair with a wooden stool.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU ASK 'SHOULDN'T YOU JUST KNOW THE ERROR CODE?'...
bullets: We do not memorize 16-character hexadecimal STOP codes. We are technicians, not encyclopedias.
Our superpower is not knowing every answer; it is knowing exactly how to interrogate a search engine to translate machine-screaming into English.
0x80070005 just means Windows is throwing a tantrum about permissions. Again.
Note: Expecting us to recite Event Viewer logs from memory will result in a long, unblinking stare until you walk away.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU DEPLOY YOUR 'YOUTUBE EXPERT' RELATIVE...
bullets: Watching a 15-minute tech vlog does not equal a decade of real-world troubleshooting experience.
Successfully plugging in an RGB LED strip once does not make someone a network topology architect.
Your cousin's "system optimizer" downloaded from a shady forum thread is just malware in a trench coat.
Note: When their "quick 5-minute fix" inevitably bricks the machine, the 'I Told You So' re-imaging fee will be applied to your department.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU TELL US WHAT 'YOUR NEPHEW WHO KNOWS COMPUTERS' SAID...
bullets: Your nephew's YouTube tutorial on running random PowerShell scripts does not apply to our network.
We will not grant you local admin rights just because a blog post said it would make your system faster.
We spent weeks configuring those VLANs; do not plug your rogue $15 unmanaged switch into the wall port.
Note: Unauthorized "Shadow IT" projects will be aggressively dismantled and returned to you in a cardboard box.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU FLEX YOUR 'IT DEGREE' ON THE HELP DESK...
bullets: Your textbook assumed a perfect, sterile environment where users actually read prompts. Welcome to the jungle.
Certifications are cute, but they don't teach you how to resurrect a server rack that was used as a coffee table.
Theory is knowing how a VLAN should route. Experience is knowing the user plugged a loopback cable into the wall port because "it looked neat."
Note: Book smarts will not save you when the unmanaged 10-year-old switch in the ceiling drops the entire subnet.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU SAY 'BUT I WATCHED YOU FIX IT LAST TIME'...
bullets: Watching me run a script does not mean you understand what the script did, why it was necessary, or what dependencies it relied upon.
A mechanic changing your oil in front of you does not qualify you to rebuild the transmission in your driveway.
"I tried to do what you did, but now it's a black screen" is the most expensive sentence you can possibly utter in this shop.
Note: The "I Tried To Fix It Myself" surcharge is automatically applied to any machine that arrives in more pieces than it started with.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BRING ME YOUR 'DIY SMART LIGHTING' PROJECT...
bullets: I do not care that your ESP32 ARGB zigzag matrix looked great when it was just sitting on a breadboard.
Splicing a 5V LED strip directly into a generic power supply without a proper standalone controller or a logic level shifter is not 'inventive,' it is an active fire hazard.
No, I will not re-solder your melted, pocket-sized offline WLED project back together for you. Please learn Ohm's Law.
Note: Just because your custom circuit fits neatly into a 3D-printed project box does not mean it won't burn your house down.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BRING IN YOUR 'BROKEN' 3D PRINTER...
bullets: A clogged nozzle on your cheap Creality or Elegoo is a rite of passage, not a critical hardware failure for the helpdesk.
I manage software deployments and network topography. I am not a mechanic for robotic hot glue guns that move in three dimensions.
Re-level your bed. Clean your build plate. Dry your filament. Stop bothering me.
Note: Bringing me an extruder completely encased in a solid, basketball-sized "blob of death" of hardened PETG plastic is grounds for a lifetime ban from this shop.

title: Support Etiquette, Remote Sessions & Client Horror
description: Support Etiquette, Remote Sessions & Client Horror

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU CALL FOR 'JUST A QUICK QUESTION'...
bullets: "Just a quick question" is almost never quick, and it is rarely just a question.
If the answer requires me remotely logging into your server, running diagnostics, and untangling a database, it is not a question; it is a "Billable Consultation."
Ambushing a technician on their lunch break or sending a WhatsApp at 9 PM does not bypass the invoicing system.
Note: Quick questions will be answered with exclusively quick, unhelpful answers. (e.g., "Is the network broken?" "Yes.")

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU FIGHT ME FOR THE MOUSE DURING A REMOTE SUPPORT SESSION...
bullets: When your cursor starts moving on its own after you called me for help, that is me.
Take your hand off the mouse. Stop touching the trackpad.
Every time you aggressively try to close the command prompt I just opened, you add ten minutes to your resolution time.
Note: This is a remote troubleshooting session, not a co-op video game. I do not need a player two.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU WALK AWAY DURING A REMOTE SUPPORT SESSION...
bullets: Do not accept the remote connection prompt and then immediately close the laptop lid to "go to lunch."
My connection to your machine is not telepathy; it requires the device to actually be powered on and awake.
Staring at a "Target Offline" error on my tablet while you email me from your phone complaining that the issue isn't fixed yet is a special kind of psychological torture.
Note: Abandoning your machine mid-troubleshooting means your ticket will be routed into an automated workflow from which it may never return.

warnings.title: BEFORE WE START YOUR REMOTE SUPPORT SESSION...
bullets: When I ask you to download the remote support tool, do not reply with "I'm not good with computers." That is literally the entire reason you are paying me.
Do not schedule a remote session and then drive to the grocery store. I cannot troubleshoot your device while it sits completely alone on your kitchen counter.
Yes, I need the 9-digit connection code. No, the code is not "password."
Note: Staring blankly at the screen while I repeat "Please click Allow" for the fourth time will result in the session timing out, along with my patience.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU QUESTION MY REMOTE SUPPORT SETUP...
bullets: Yes, I am fixing your infrastructure from a custom Android launcher on my Galaxy Tab. No, that does not mean I am 'playing games' instead of working.
I spent hours optimizing my entire mobile SSH workflow specifically so I can rescue your business while I am not even at a desk.
Please do not critique my tools when your primary network admin password is on a sticky note taped to the monitor.
Note: If you insist on waiting until I am 'at a real computer' to let me fix it, your ticket automatically goes to the back of the queue.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU ASK FOR 'LIFETIME FREE SUPPORT'...
bullets: Replacing your hard drive five years ago does not mean I am now your personal, unpaid digital butler for the rest of eternity.
I have been doing this for over a decade. I know what natural hardware wear-and-tear looks like, and I know what 'I dropped it in the driveway' looks like.
My warranty covers the parts I installed, not the malware you intentionally bypassed Chrome's warnings to download.
Note: "But you're the last one who touched it" is a legally non-binding statement that will be met with an immediate dial tone.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU TELL ME 'IT SHOULD BE A FIVE MINUTE JOB'...
bullets: If it was a five-minute job, you would have done it yourself.
We both know that 'just looking at the Wi-Fi' is actually going to uncover a nested web of unauthorized switches, IP conflicts, and a rogue DHCP server someone plugged in for fun.
Do not dictate the timeline of a technical diagnosis before I have even opened the terminal.
Note: Every time you say "It should be an easy fix," an additional emotional damage surcharge is silently added to the final invoice.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU ARGUE ABOUT THE INVOICE...
bullets: You are not paying R800 for the single line of PowerShell code I typed.
You are paying for the years of suffering it took for me to know exactly which line of code would fix your registry without vaporizing your operating system.
My diagnosis fee is non-negotiable. "But you didn't even replace any parts!" is not a valid counter-argument when I just spent two hours undoing your nephew's handiwork.
Note: Refusal to pay the "Stupidity Tax" means your device will be held hostage as a paperweight until the balance is cleared.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU DECLARE A 'BUSINESS-CRITICAL EMERGENCY'...
bullets: If the issue has been happening for six months, it is not an emergency just because you finally got annoyed by it at 4:55 PM on a Friday.
Screaming "I am losing thousands of Rands a minute!" does not make the Windows update progress bar move any faster.
A genuine drop-everything emergency response requires an emergency invoice.
Note: Curiously, 90% of 'critical emergencies' immediately downgrade to 'we can look at it next week' the exact second the emergency billing rate is mentioned.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU THREATEN ME WITH A 'BAD REVIEW'...
bullets: Go ahead. But know that I contribute heavily to the Local Guides program, I understand exactly how the review algorithms work, and your unhinged 1-star rant will be flagged and ghosted before I even finish my coffee.
Leaving a bad review because you are mad you had to pay standard customs clearance and import taxes on a sketchy parcel you shipped from overseas is peak delusion.
I control the network, the backups, and the firewall. A Google Maps review is the absolute least of your worries.
Note: Extortion is not a valid troubleshooting step.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU PASTE THAT AI-GENERATED SCRIPT INTO POWERSHELL...
bullets: A language model is essentially a highly confident autocomplete. It does not know our network topology, it does not understand our firewall rules, and it certainly does not care if it vaporizes the active directory.
If the AI hallucinates a command and tells you to delete a core registry key to "optimize performance," and you blindly hit 'Enter', you are not a programmer. You are a digital liability.

Unless you actually know how to code, or at the very least have an n8n workflow safely archiving your technical prompts and responses into Notion so we can audit the disaster, step away from the terminal.
Note: "But the chatbot said it was perfectly safe" is a defense that will be laughed out of the server room.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU SUBMIT A TICKET FOR THE 'CUSTOM APP' THE AI BUILT YOU...
bullets: Prompting a web interface to "build a billing system in Python" and receiving 400 lines of disjointed, hallucinated spaghetti code does not make you a software developer.
The AI just invented three libraries that do not exist in this universe and forgot to include a database connection.

I will not debug your digital alphabet soup. If you aren't spinning up a local LLM via Ollama to actually test and isolate your own code in a controlled environment, do not bring your compilation errors to my desk.
Note: My hourly rate triples the exact second I have to read code written by a robot that forgot how math works.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU PANIC THAT 'AI HACKERS' CLONED YOUR IDENTITY...
bullets: You are not a high-level corporate executive, and no international cyber syndicate is spending computing power to train a voice cloning model on your Microsoft Teams meetings.

Yes, voice cloning technology exists — it is great for passion projects like making an Arlecchino voice model for a gaming mod — but the scammer who called you is just playing a generic MP3 recording of a person coughing. They did not synthesize your voice.
Stop clicking on Facebook ads for "Free Crypto," and your identity will magically remain secure.
Note: The biggest threat to your personal data is not an artificial superintelligence; it is your own inability to recognize a phishing email.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU USE AI TO 'SUMMARIZE' COMPANY DOCUMENTS...
bullets: Pasting highly confidential, proprietary client financial data into a public web chatbot so you don't have to read a 10-page PDF is a catastrophic breach of security.
You are actively training an external corporation's language model on our private company secrets.
Furthermore, the AI just hallucinated an entire paragraph about a merger that isn't happening because it got confused by a similar article from 2018. Now you look like an idiot in the board meeting.
Note: Using a language model to do your reading comprehension for you will result in your immediate transfer to a department that primarily uses crayons.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU DEMAND I FIX THE AI'S 'FACTUAL ERROR'...
bullets: I am an IT Technician. I manage the physical hardware and the local network. I am not the lead developer at OpenAI, Google, or Anthropic.

If the chatbot confidently tells you that the capital of France is "Cheese," I cannot "go into the system and correct it." I do not control the multi-billion-parameter neural network housed in a server farm in California.
Stop submitting helpdesk tickets because a language model lost an argument with you.
Note: Arguing with an algorithm is a symptom of madness. Forcing your IT department to participate in that argument is grounds for termination.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU ASK ME TO 'PUT AI' ON YOUR OFFICE MACHINE...
bullets: Running a local Large Language Model via Ollama requires actual, dedicated hardware, not a six-year-old Celeron processor gasping for air.
"AI" is not magic. It cannot summarize your spreadsheets if your machine doesn't even have the memory to open the spreadsheet in the first place.
Also, your device's voice assistant is not "listening to your thoughts" or "hearing" you like a human. It receives processed text converted from your mumbling. Speak clearly.
Note: Asking for 'the ChatGPT' to be installed on your network router will result in me staring at you in profound, unblinking silence.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU YELL THAT 'THE AI ISN'T WORKING'...
bullets: Paying your monthly fee for Google One storage just means you bought a bigger bucket to hoard your unorganized junk files.
It does NOT grant you paid-tier access to the Gemini API.
You cannot try to run enterprise-grade data analysis on a rate-limited endpoint and then scream at me when the system tells you to slow down.
Note: Read your own subscription invoices before you open a high-priority ticket complaining about a service you literally do not pay for.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU RELY ON 'THOUGHTS AND PRAYERS' TO FIX YOUR HARDWARE...
bullets: God is not a network administrator. He will not assign you a static IP address just because you asked nicely.
Holy water immediately and permanently voids the manufacturer's warranty. Do not sprinkle things on the motherboard.
If your IT infrastructure relies entirely on "a wing and a prayer," you belong in a monastery, not a server room.
Note: When the Blue Screen of Death appears, no amount of spiritual bargaining will recover that 40-page unsaved spreadsheet.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU TELL ME 'HOPEFULLY IT WORKS THIS TIME'...
bullets: "Hope" is not a recognized troubleshooting methodology. I do not deal in hope; I deal in Ping, TraceRt, and error logs.
Hope is what you have to use when you haven't tested your server backups since 2019.
I didn't spend a decade staring at terminal windows, reading hex codes, and rebuilding networks to just "hope" a script executes properly.
Note: If our strategy is officially reduced to hoping, my standard hourly rate transitions into a 'Miracle Worker' retainer, which is significantly more expensive.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU QUESTION THE DIAGNOSIS BECAUSE YOU 'HAVE A GOOD FEELING'...
bullets: Your intuition did not pay for my experience, the countless hours spent fixing broken arrays, or the caffeine required to survive this industry.
My diagnostic report is not an opening offer for negotiation. It is a forensic autopsy of your poor technological decisions.
Telling me "let's just wait and see if it fixes itself" is the digital equivalent of ignoring a check engine light while driving headfirst into the Karoo.
Note: When your "good feeling" inevitably ends in total system failure, the "I Told You So" emergency response fee will be aggressively applied.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU ATTEMPT A DIGITAL EXORCISM ON YOUR WORKSTATION...
bullets: Your machine is not possessed by a demon; it is possessed by 47 malicious browser extensions you downloaded to get free coupon codes.
Smudging sage in the server room does not cleanse the network of bad vibes; it triggers the fire suppression system and destroys half a million Rands worth of switches.
Screaming at the monitor in tongues will not fix the corrupted registry, but it will make HR open a file on you.
Note: Unless the printer actually starts bleeding ink and speaking Aramaic, do not declare a spiritual emergency. Just submit a standard ticket.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU TELL ME 'IT'S A MIRACLE' THAT I FIXED IT...
bullets: It was not a miracle. It was three hours of grueling, meticulous command-line surgery while you were at lunch.
Calling it a miracle implies that it just magically happened, completely undermining the sheer force of will it took to undo the digital knot you tied.
Miracles are free. My time, expertise, and refusal to let a machine defeat me are strictly billable.
Note: Praise is appreciated, but paying the invoice on time is the highest form of worship an IT Technician can receive.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU CLAIM 'THE UNIVERSE IS AGAINST YOU'...
bullets: Computers are literally just refined sand and metal that we tricked into thinking by trapping lightning inside them. They are physically incapable of malice or holding a grudge against you.
The universe is not targeting your specific workstation. You are just aggressively clicking a flashing banner that says "Download Free RAM."
Mercury being in retrograde has absolutely zero effect on your local area network's packet loss.
Note: Karma does not cause catastrophic hardware failure; user error does.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU USE YOUR 'LIFE EXPERIENCE' AS A CREDENTIAL...
bullets: Being 60 years old and "knowing how the real world works" does not grant you an innate, mystical understanding of how a Linux Ubuntu server mounts a Docker volume.
I respect your eldership, but your decades of general life experience do not override my actual, hands-on IT trauma from rebuilding corrupted arrays since 2013.
"Back in my day we didn't have these problems" is correct, because back in your day you used a typewriter that didn't require a constant ping to a cloud server to verify its license key.
Note: General wisdom comes with age. Knowledge of the Windows Print Spooler comes strictly from unrelenting suffering.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU START YOUR 'DIGITAL CONFESSION'...
bullets: I am an IT Technician, not a priest. I do not care about your moral purity, and I am not here to judge the depths of your soul.
I just need you to admit exactly which sketchy hyperlink you clicked so I can isolate the payload before it hits the company server.
However, if you look me in the eye, swear on a holy text that you "didn't spill anything," and I open the chassis to find a sticky puddle of dried Oros... we are going to have a serious problem.
Note: Lying under oath in the IT room instantly voids your warranty and doubles the diagnostic fee.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU DEMAND I LINK YOUR FNB ACCOUNT TO PAYPAL 'FOR FREE'...
bullets: I am an IT Technician. I manage hardware and networks. I am not a certified financial planner, a forex trader, or a wizard.
If the actual, paid tellers at First National Bank stare at you blankly when you ask how to link the accounts, what makes you think I possess a secret backdoor into the international banking sector?

It requires navigating the labyrinth of FNB online banking, dealing with Reserve Bank mandates, and paying exchange rate fees. No, it is not "free." You are moving money across the planet. The bank wants its cut, and my hourly rate to watch you fail to remember your banking PIN five times in a row still applies.
Note: If you lock your banking profile during this process, do not hand me the phone. I will not go to prison for your financial illiteracy.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU COMPLAIN THAT YOUR HOME WI-FI IS 'BROKEN AND SLOW'...
bullets: You live in a house with four human beings. You deliberately chose to pay for a bare-minimum 20Mbps internet package. Please consult a primary school mathematics textbook.

Let's do the math: Someone is downloading a 120GB game update, someone else is streaming 4K Netflix, someone is on a Zoom call, and there are six cellphones silently syncing background data. You do not have a "network issue." You have a traffic jam caused by your own cheapness.
20 Megabits per second divided by 14 active smart devices equals buffering, suffering, and pixelated misery. The router is not broken; it is crying out for mercy.
Note: Upgrading your ISP package costs money. Screaming at me that "we should all be able to use it at once" is free, but it defies the laws of physics and will be ignored.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BUY 15 'SMART' DEVICES FOR YOUR 20MBPS NETWORK...
bullets: Every single cheap, unbranded smart plug, Wi-Fi lightbulb, and knock-off security camera you connect to that poor, overworked router takes up a slice of the bandwidth.
Your router was provided for free by your ISP in 2018. It does not have the processing power to simultaneously manage the IP addresses of your entire family's devices plus your Wi-Fi kettle.
When your internet completely collapses because your smart fridge decided to run a firmware update while you were watching YouTube, that is not a cyberattack. That is a self-inflicted wound.
Note: I will not configure a custom VLAN and QoS traffic prioritization on a consumer-grade router that feels like it was made of recycled Tupperware. Buy better equipment.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU SEND AN URGENT TICKET FOR A 'BROKEN' MOUSE/KEYBOARD...
bullets: Check the battery (If wireless). Change them first.
Check if it is plugged in (If wired). Both ends.
Spilling a coffee on it (again) is user error.
Note: Our supply of PS/2 clunker keyboards is not infinite.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU SUBMIT A TICKET FOR A 'DEAD' MONITOR...
bullets: Did you press the power button on the actual monitor?
No, the power button on the computer tower does not magically turn on every peripheral in a 5-foot radius.
If the screen is black but there is a tiny amber light glowing in the bottom right corner, the display is fine. It is just deeply, deeply disappointed in you.
Note: Submitting an emergency ticket for an unplugged VGA cable will result in a mandatory "Shapes and Colors" matching test.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU ASK TO 'BORROW A CABLE REAL QUICK'...
bullets: Cables borrowed from the IT desk enter a localized black hole and cease to exist in our dimension.
An HDMI cable is not a DisplayPort cable. Pushing harder will not change the laws of physics.
Yes, we know you "just need it for a presentation."
Note: We require collateral for all loaner adapters. Car keys and firstborn children are currently accepted.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BLAME 'THE NETWORK' FOR YOUR MISSED DEADLINES...
bullets: I can see the active resource monitor. You weren't compiling code; you were streaming anime and reading manga.
Claiming "network latency" caused your work delay is a bold move when the firewall logs show you actively trying to 100% the new Genshin Impact map on company time.
If you submit an urgent hardware ticket because your machine crashed right as you deployed Chevruse in the Abyss, I will personally throttle your workstation's bandwidth to dial-up speeds.
Note: Lying about your desktop activity while I hold the router logs is like arguing with the grim reaper. You will lose.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU ASK ME TO PAY YOUR SABC TV LICENSE...
bullets: I fix computers. I manage Docker containers and Linux servers. I do not manage your personal statutory obligations or your tax returns.
A monitor is not a television. If you bought an actual TV to use as a display and the government is after you for the license fee, that is entirely your fault.
Do not forward me the billing emails from the broadcasting corporation asking "is this a scam?" Pay your bills.
Note: The IT Department is not your financial advisor, your lawyer, or your mother.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU SAY 'IT COMPILES ON MY MACHINE'...
bullets: Your machine is a chaotic petri dish of mismatched dependencies, disabled firewalls, and a Python environment that hasn't been cleaned since 2019.
The production server is not your personal development sandbox. It runs a clean, immutable OS. If it doesn't run there, it doesn't run anywhere.
"It compiles" is the bare minimum of achievement. Does it run? Does it scale? Does it randomly delete the user table at 3 AM?
Note: A Docker container that explodes on deploy because you hardcoded your local file paths is a you problem, not an ops problem.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU SAY 'I'LL FIX IT IN PROD'...
bullets: No. Absolutely not. Production is not your staging environment, your testing playground, or your "let's see what happens" lab.
Pushing untested code directly to the live branch at 4:55 PM on a Friday is how you earn a permanent ban from the deployment pipeline.
The audit trail exists. We will know it was you. The rollback script is already written and waiting.
Note: "I'll fix it in prod" is the battle cry of someone who has never been woken up at 3 AM by a pager duty alert.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU CLAIM 'THAT'S NOT A BUG, IT'S A FEATURE'...
bullets: If the undocumented behavior corrupts the database silently, it is not a feature. It is a liability.
Hiding broken functionality behind "intentional design choices" is not clever; it is fraudulent software development.
We have users actively filing tickets. The screenshots are timestamped. Your gaslighting does not survive contact with evidence.
Note: Calling a crash "an unscheduled system restart for security hardening" will not save you from the post-mortem.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU SUBMIT CODE WITHOUT RUNNING THE TESTS...
bullets: "I forgot to run the tests" translates to "I don't care if I broke everything."
A pull request that fails CI/CD checks is not a pull request; it is a donation of broken code to the repository.
Every time you skip linting, a production server somewhere silently weeps.
Note: If your response to a failing test is "comment it out so it passes," you are not a developer. You are a code vandal.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU MERGE WITHOUT A CODE REVIEW...
bullets: Your code is not perfect. You are not an exception to the rule. Everyone needs a second pair of eyes.
Merging your own pull request directly into main without so much as a glance from a peer is not confidence; it is recklessness.
The person who breaks the build and then pushes a "fix" that breaks it further does not get to complain about the rollback process.
Note: We do not trust the person who introduced a SQL injection vulnerability because they "didn't think it mattered."

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU HARDCODE A SECRET INTO THE SOURCE...
bullets: An API key in plaintext, committed to a public repository, is not a configuration strategy. It is a data breach waiting to happen.
"I'll encrypt it later" is the same energy as "I'll fix it in prod."
Git history is forever. Even after you remove the secret, it lives in the commit logs for anyone with a search engine to find.
Note: Rotating credentials because you couldn't be bothered to use environment variables is a waste of everyone's time.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU DEPLOY 'ONE SMALL HOTFIX' ON A FRIDAY NIGHT...
bullets: The "small hotfix" will cascade. It will touch something unrelated. It will bring down the entire microservices architecture.
Friday 4:55 PM deployments are statistically the leading cause of ruined weekends for DevOps teams.
If it absolutely cannot wait until Monday, the change request must be signed in blood and approved by three separate teams.
Note: There is no such thing as a "quick" deployment. There are only deployments that haven't broken anything yet.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU COMPLAIN ABOUT THE CODE REVIEW COMMENTS...
bullets: I am not "nitpicking." I am ensuring the next person who inherits your spaghetti nightmare can actually read it.
Variable names like `data`, `data2`, `dataFinal`, `dataFinal_ACTUAL`, and `dataFinal_ACTUAL_v2` are not descriptive. They are a cry for help.
A 2,000-line function with no comments and 14 levels of nested conditionals is not "legacy." It is archaeological debris.
Note: If you feel personally attacked by a linter, this industry may not be for you.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BLAME 'MERGE CONFLICTS' ON THE TEAM...
bullets: Merge conflicts happen when two people edit the same code simultaneously. They are not a personal attack on your workflow.
Screaming "just accept mine" without reviewing the diff is how critical logic gets silently deleted.
If every single one of your branches results in apocalyptic merge conflicts, the common denominator is standing right in front of the keyboard.
Note: Yelling at Git will not resolve the conflict. It will, however, make the rest of the team question your emotional stability.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU PUSH A DEPENDENCY UPDATE WITHOUT TESTING...
bullets: Updating a package because "it was the latest version" without reading the changelog or running the test suite is a gamble with production stability.
That minor version bump you just pushed introduces a breaking change to a completely unrelated module because of transitive dependencies.
"But it passed on my machine" does not cover the 200 integration tests you didn't run.
Note: npm update, pip install --upgrade, and blind faith are not a deployment strategy.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BRING ME A DRIVE THAT'S BEEN 'MAKING A FUNNY NOISE FOR MONTHS'...
bullets: That "funny noise" is the sound of the read/write head physically scraping across the platter. It is not a quirky personality trait of your hard drive.
A clicking hard drive is not "still working fine." It is performing its death rattle.
You had months to back up your data. You chose not to. Now the drive is beyond recovery without spending more than the data is worth.
Note: No, we cannot "just glue the platter back together." That is not how any of this works.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU ASK WHY THE 'OLD SPARE' PC WON'T BOOT...
bullets: That machine has been sitting in a damp store room for six years. The CMOS battery has expired, the thermal paste is the consistency of chalk, and the PSU capacitors are bulging like they're about to give birth.
"It was working fine when we put it away" — yes, and a car left in a field for a decade was "driving fine" when it was parked.
You cannot deploy a 15-year-old Core 2 Duo with 2GB of DDR2 RAM and expect it to run Windows 11. You cannot even expect it to run a calculator without audible suffering.
Note: The "spare" PC is not a spare. It is an archaeological artifact.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU COMPLAIN THAT THE 'NEW' SECOND-HAND SERVER IS LOUD...
bullets: Enterprise server fans are not designed to be quiet. They are designed to move enough air to cool a small furnace.
That Delta fan screaming at 10,000 RPM is not broken. It is working exactly as intended. Your expectations are what is broken.
A server rack belongs in a soundproofed server room, not wedged under someone's desk in the open-plan office.
Note: If you wanted silent, you should have bought a laptop. If you wanted enterprise compute, you accept the jet engine noises.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU HAND ME A USB DRIVE THAT HAS BEEN THROUGH WAR...
bullets: This USB drive has lived in your pocket with loose change, been washed in a jeans cycle, dipped in coffee, and used as a keychain for three years.
It has been plugged into 47 different machines across 4 continents, accumulating malware like a digital venereal disease.
"All my important files are on here, it's my only copy" — then why is it treated like a lost luggage tag?
Note: A USB drive is temporary storage, not a permanent backup solution. Especially not one held together by sheer hope and corrosion.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BRING IN A POWER SUPPLY THAT 'POPPED'...
bullets: That loud bang and magic blue smoke was the PSU sacrificing itself to protect your components. Be grateful, not annoyed.
No, we cannot "just fix the blown capacitor." A PSU that failed once will fail again, and next time it might take the entire motherboard with it.
Buying the cheapest no-name PSU on Takealot because "it's just power" is how you turn your entire PC into a paperweight.
Note: A PSU is not a component you cheap out on. It is the single point of failure for your entire machine. Respect the power supply.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU ASK TO RECOVER DATA FROM A DRIVE THAT WAS REFORMATTED...
bullets: "I accidentally formatted the wrong drive" is a sentence that should never be uttered by anyone who values their data.
The more you use the machine after formatting, the more of the old data gets overwritten. Every second counts.
No, running a quick format and then installing a fresh OS on top does not make recovery "easier." It makes it nearly impossible.
Note: Data recovery is expensive, time-consuming, and never guaranteed. The only "recovery" strategy that works is having a backup before you break it.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BLAME THE 'POWER SURGE' FOR EVERYTHING...
bullets: A proper surge protector costs less than a pizza. If your equipment is plugged directly into the wall, you are gambling with fire.
Yes, a surge can kill a device instantly. No, that does not explain why the screen is cracked.
Lightning strikes are rare. Dropping your laptop off your desk is not. Stop blaming the weather.
Note: If every single one of your devices dies a "mysterious electrical death" while your neighbor's identical setup is fine, check your own wiring before calling IT.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU ASK TO REPURPOSE THE 'OFFICE PRINTER' FROM 2005...
bullets: That printer connects via parallel port. Your modern laptop does not have a parallel port. An adapter exists, but it will not make the printer work.
The drivers were last updated for Windows XP. They do not exist for Windows 11. They will never exist.
"Can't you just make it work?" — I can, by setting up a dedicated Windows XP VM with a passthrough parallel port, and you will not like the hourly rate for that configuration.
Note: Some hardware belongs in a museum, not on your network. Let it go.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BUY A LAPTOP FROM A 'GREAT DEAL' ONLINE...
bullets: If the price is too good to be true, the laptop is either stolen, refurbished with non-genuine parts, or a counterfeit running a skin over Android.
"Intel Core i7" means nothing when it is a 12-year-old low-voltage mobile chip from a scrapped lineup.
No, you cannot return it because "it's slow." You bought a device with 4GB of RAM and eMMC storage in 2026. What precisely did you expect?
Note: The cheapest listing on PriceCheck is not a "hack." It is a trap.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU ORDER A CHARGER FROM A SHADY WEBSITE...
bullets: That R79 "universal laptop charger" will absolutely charge your laptop. Once. Then it will either melt, catch fire, or deliver a dirty voltage spike that kills the charging IC permanently.
A genuine charger costs what it costs because it contains proper voltage regulation, shielding, and safety certifications. The knock-off contains hopes, dreams, and loose solder joints.
"It fits the port" is not the same as "it is electrically compatible with this device."
Note: Saving R200 on a charger today costs you R8,000 for a new motherboard tomorrow. Your choice.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BUY A 'SERVER-GRADE' DESKTOP PC FROM A LIQUIDATION SALE...
bullets: That enterprise workstation you picked up for a "steal" is a Dell Precision from 2016 with a Xeon CPU that draws 165W at idle and sounds like a hair dryer.
It came with Windows 7. Upgrading it to Windows 11 requires bypassing every hardware guard Microsoft designed. It will not be stable.
The previous company decommissioned it for a reason. That reason was not "it was too powerful."
Note: Ex-corporate hardware is cheap for a reason. That reason is electricity bills and fan noise that will make your home office uninhabitable.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BUY A MONITOR WITHOUT CHECKING THE INPUTS...
bullets: You just bought a gorgeous 4K monitor with no HDMI ports. Only VGA. In 2026.
"I thought all monitors had HDMI" is an expensive assumption.
Yes, we have an adapter. No, the adapter will not make it look good. VGA on a 4K panel looks like a impressionist painting of a spreadsheet.
Note: Check the I/O panel before you click "Buy." We cannot return opened electronics for "my mistake."

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU ASK WHY THE 'INDUSTRIAL' ROUTER WON'T WORK AT HOME...
bullets: That enterprise-grade Cisco/Mikrotik router you bought second-hand was designed for a data center with a dedicated network engineer on staff.
The configuration interface is a command line with no hand-holding. There is no "wizard" mode. There is no "plug and play."
"Can't you just set it up quickly?" — I can, but the 47 firewall rules, VLAN segmentation, and BGP routing you don't need will still be running in the background consuming electricity.
Note: Buying enterprise gear because it was "cheaper than a Asus router" is like buying a freight truck because it was cheaper than a hatchback. It will not fit in your garage.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU IMPORT ELECTRONICS WITHOUT CHECKING THE PLUG...
bullets: That American-specification server you imported runs on 110V. Our walls deliver 230V. Plugging it in directly will result in an immediate and spectacular fireworks display.
A step-down transformer is heavy, expensive, and generates heat. It is not a "simple adapter."
No amount of praying to the electrical gods will make 230V equal 110V. Physics does not negotiate.
Note: South Africa uses 230V with a Type M plug. Check the voltage rating before you click "Ship to South Africa."

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BUY A 'BUNDLE' DEAL WITH UNMATCHED COMPONENTS...
bullets: "Intel motherboard with AMD CPU" — these are not compatible. They have never been compatible. They will never be compatible.
The pins are different. The sockets are different. The electrical signalling is different. It is not a "minor incompatibility."
"But the seller said they work together" — the seller is a liar who has already received your money and blocked your number.
Note: CPU and motherboard compatibility is not a matter of opinion. It is a matter of physics. Do not trust a listing that contradicts physics.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BUY A PRINTER BASED SOLELY ON THE PRICE OF THE PRINTER...
bullets: Printers are not sold at a loss out of generosity. They are sold at a loss because the manufacturer intends to recoup the margin through ink cartridge sales.
That R399 printer will consume R2,000 worth of ink in the first year. The cartridges will have half the ink volume of the standard size and cost the same.
"But it's cheap to buy" — yes, and a free puppy is also cheap until you realize the cost of feeding it.
Note: A cheap printer is the most expensive printer you can buy. Do the math on ink cost per page before purchasing.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BUY A 'GAMING' LAPTOP AS A "PORTABLE WORKSTATION"...
bullets: Gaming laptops are not portable workstations. They are desktop replacements with a battery that lasts 45 minutes.
The "gaming" tax means you paid extra for RGB lighting, a chassis that looks like a transformer, and fans loud enough to drown out a lawnmower.
For the same price, a business-class Ultrabook would be lighter, quieter, faster at productivity tasks, and last 8 hours on battery.
Note: Buying a gaming laptop for Excel and email is like buying a Ferrari to drive to the post office. Impressive, but deeply impractical.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU TELL ME YOUR 'CYBERSECURITY RESEARCH'...
bullets: Reading one article about the latest zero-day vulnerability does not make you a cybersecurity analyst. It makes you informed. There is a difference.
No, that vulnerability does not apply to our environment. We patched it three months ago. You are the last person to hear about it.
Forwarding a sensationalist news headline to the entire company with "ARE WE SAFE?!" is not security awareness. It is panic marketing.
Note: If the article came from a pop-up ad, it is not journalism. It is malware advertising disguised as a warning.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU DEMAND AN 'IMMEDIATE SECURITY REVIEW' AFTER ONE NEWS STORY...
bullets: That single Bloomberg article about a new attack vector did not instantly invalidate our entire security posture.
Our firewall rules, endpoint detection, and patch management pipeline were not designed by people who read one article.
If you are suddenly concerned about security, start by not using "Password123" for your corporate login.
Note: A sudden interest in cybersecurity because you watched a Netflix documentary does not grant you override authority over the IT security policy.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU FOLLOW ADVICE FROM A 'TECH BLOG' YOU FOUND ON FACEBOOK...
bullets: That article recommending you "disable Windows Defender for better performance" was written by someone who does not understand security.
"10 Registry Hacks to Speed Up Your PC" is how you end up with a machine that cannot boot.
No, deleting System32 will not "free up valuable disk space." It will destroy your operating system. This is not a prank. It is reality.
Note: If the article is hosted on a site that also sells weight loss gummies, perhaps do not apply its technical advice to your work machine.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU CLAIM 'THE INTERNET SAID THIS IS THE BEST ANTIVIRUS'...
bullets: The "Top 10 Antivirus Software" list you read was a paid advertisement. Every single entry paid to be on that list.
The best antivirus is the one centrally managed by the IT department and pushed to your machine automatically.
Installing a second, third, or fourth antivirus "just to be safe" actually makes you less safe. They conflict, crash, and leave gaps.
Note: If your antivirus was advertised during a YouTube preroll, it is probably not the best option.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU USE A 'PRIVACY TIP' FROM A FORUM...
bullets: Some random Reddit user's advice to "disable all telemetry via a script from this pastebin" is not a privacy strategy. It is an infection vector.
"I found this tool that blocks all Microsoft tracking" — and that tool also blocks your ability to receive security updates. Congratulations.
Forum advice is not vetted. It is not peer-reviewed. It is someone's opinion typed into a text box at 2 AM.
Note: No, you cannot name a child "Null" to bypass login screens. That stopped working a decade ago. Stop trying.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU PANIC ABOUT A 'CRITICAL ALERT' POP-UP...
bullets: "Your computer is infected! Call this number immediately!" is a scam. A real antivirus does not demand you call a toll-free number.
Full-screen browser pop-ups that mimic Windows system alerts are not legitimate. They are social engineering.
The "Your license has expired!" notification that asks for your credit card to renew? Not from us. We do not charge you to use the company laptop.
Note: If the alert asks for payment in iTunes gift cards, it is not a security warning. It is a comedy of errors waiting to happen.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU QUOTE AN ARTICLE ABOUT HOW 'WI-FI CAUSES HEALTH ISSUES'...
bullets: That study was debunked, retracted, and the author was found to have fabricated data. It is not a credible source.
Wi-Fi uses non-ionizing radiation. It does not cause cancer, brain damage, or attract insects. It just moves data through the air.
If you are genuinely concerned, the solution is not to demand we disable the Wi-Fi for the entire office. It is to educate yourself on basic physics.
Note: The electromagnetic field from your Wi-Fi router is weaker than the natural background radiation you are exposed to during a single flight to Cape Town.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BRING UP 'THAT ARTICLE ABOUT THE GOOGLE EMPLOYEE MONITORING'...
bullets: Yes, major tech companies collect data. This has been known since the early 2000s. It is not a breaking news revelation.

No, they are not listening to your private conversations through your phone's microphone to serve you ads. That would be illegal, impractical, and unnecessary. They already have enough data from your search history.
Sharing a sensationalist headline from 2018 as if it just dropped today does not make you a privacy advocate. It makes you late to the conversation.
Note: If you are truly concerned about privacy, start by reading the terms of service for the apps you already installed. The answer is always in the fine print.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU TELL ME 'A FRIEND OF A FRIEND SAID...'
bullets: Secondhand technical advice from someone who knows someone who "works in IT" is not a reliable source.
"My cousin's roommate fixed the same issue by deleting this file" — and your cousin's roommate's fix is why your machine is now also broken.
Referral advice is not documentation. If it cannot be verified by a reputable source, it does not belong on a company device.
Note: The friend of a friend who "works in IT" may be the same person who thinks the "any key" is a real button on the keyboard.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BLAME THE CAT FOR YOUR DEAD HARD DRIVE...
bullets: I have heard "my cat walked across the keyboard" approximately 400 times. I have yet to meet a cat that can navigate to diskpart and type "clean."
Pets shed fur. They do not execute PowerShell scripts, delete system32, or reconfigure your network adapter.
If your cat genuinely caused the damage, there will be visible evidence. Not a cleanly formatted drive with all your "important business files" mysteriously erased.
Note: Blaming the pet voids the pet's innocence and insults our intelligence simultaneously.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU CLAIM YOUR TODDLER 'DELETED THE COMPANY FILES'...
bullets: Your two-year-old may be advanced, but not advanced enough to navigate to the server share, authenticate with your saved credentials, and perform a selective deletion of only the critical quarterly reports.
Children bang on keyboards. They produce gibberish. They do not produce a neatly emptied recycle bin.
If your child is genuinely that skilled, put them through college and stop wasting their talent on destroying your department budget.
Note: "My kid did it" is the new "the dog ate my homework." Except this time it is R50,000 worth of forensic data recovery.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU SAY YOUR PET 'CHEWED THROUGH THE CABLE'...
bullets: Yes, pets chew cables. But they do not chew through fibre optic patch cables, HDMI cables, and a power cord simultaneously while leaving the Ethernet cable perfectly intact.
The tooth marks on your power brick are suspiciously uniform.
If your pet did chew through it, why did you wait three months to report it?
Note: Lying about pet damage is a crime against both IT and animal-kind. The cat does not deserve this slander.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU BLAME THE CLEANING STAFF...
bullets: The cleaning staff vacuums around your desk. They do not unplug the server, wipe your hard drive, or steal your mouse.
"The cleaner must have bumped it" is the go-to excuse for every mysterious hardware failure since the invention of the office.
If your machine was fine before the cleaner arrived, the most likely explanation is they unplugged a cable and plugged it into the wrong port. That is still your fault for not labelling your cables.
Note: Stop scapegoating the cleaning staff. They are not your personal IT scapegoats.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU CLAIM 'A BUG CRAWLED INTO MY LAPTOP'...
bullets: Insects are small. They do not type denial-of-service attacks into your command prompt.
A bug in the case will cause a hardware short if you are extremely unlucky. It will not cause your Facebook account to send spam messages.
"There must be a virus" — yes, the virus is you clicking "Allow Notifications" on every sketchy website you visit.
Note: Actual bugs cause hardware failure. Digital bugs cause user-error failure. Know the difference.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU SHOW ME YOUR 'CABLE MANAGEMENT'...
bullets: A tangled nest of cables shoved behind the desk is not "managed." It is an electrified bird's nest waiting to short-circuit.
If I cannot identify which cable belongs to which device without tracing it with my finger like a detective solving a murder, you have failed.
Velcro straps exist. Cable ties exist. Labelling exists. You chose chaos.
Note: "I'll sort it out later" — later is now. I am here. Sort it out while I watch.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU CRIMP YOUR OWN ETHERNET CABLE...
bullets: That RJ45 connector you terminated has the wires in approximately the right order but the colours are in a sequence that does not appear in any known standard.
The crimp is loose. The jacket is not clamped. The exposed copper is longer than the insulation. This cable will work exactly until you need it most, then fail silently.
A factory-made patch cable costs R50. Your "homemade" cable will cost me two hours of my life diagnosing intermittent connectivity.
Note: Unless you are a certified network cabling technician, leave the crimping tool in the drawer. You are not saving money; you are creating future suffering.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU PLUG A POWER STRIP INTO ANOTHER POWER STRIP...
bullets: Daisy-chaining power strips is not "extending your reach." It is a fire hazard with extra steps.
The maximum load rating does not multiply because you plugged one strip into another. It divides. You are now operating dangerously close to thermal event territory.

Extension cords under carpets, power strips behind desks where they cannot be unplugged, and cables stretched taut across walkways are not "temporary solutions." They are OSHA violation exhibits waiting to happen.
Note: A daisy-chained power strip does not give you more power. It gives the fire department more work.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU RUN CABLE THROUGH THE CEILING TILES...
bullets: The ceiling is not a cable tray. Dropping unsecured, unrated Ethernet cable across the suspended ceiling grid is how you interfere with fire suppression sprinklers and emergency lighting.
Yes, it looks clean from below. Yes, it is a violation of every building code written since 1975.
If the ceiling tiles have to be removed for maintenance and your unmarked cable comes crashing down, I am not responsible for identifying which of the 14 unlabeled cables belongs to your department.
Note: Hidden cable is not "clean." It is "hidden." There is a difference.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU USE ZIP TIES LIKE A WEAPON...
bullets: Zip ties are for temporary bundling, not for cinching cables so tight that the inner conductors are permanently deformed.
A zip tie tightened with the force of a thousand suns does not improve cable management. It creates a point of failure where the cable will eventually break internally.
Also, do not zip-tie cables to structural pipes, gas lines, or sprinkler systems. If I have to explain why that is wrong, you should not be touching cables.
Note: Snip the zip tie flush with the head so the next person does not draw blood retrieving it. Basic human decency.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU CLAIM 'THE CABLE WAS LIKE THAT WHEN I GOT HERE'...
bullets: The cable has been there for seven years. You have been in this office for six of those years. You are not an innocent bystander; you are an accessory.
Cables do not naturally migrate, tangle themselves, or accumulate dust bunnies the size of small mammals. That is neglect.
Every time you plug and unplug a USB cable by yanking the cord instead of the connector, you shorten its lifespan. One day it will stop working. That day is your fault.
Note: Cable entropy is not a law of physics. It is a law of laziness.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU SEND A VOICE NOTE TO THE IT DESK...
bullets: I cannot troubleshoot a DNS resolution failure from a 47-second voice note recorded in a wind tunnel.
"The thingy is not working" delivered via voice note at 2 AM is not a support request. It is a noise complaint.
Text is searchable. Voice notes are not. If you need me to remember what you said next week, type it.
Note: A voice note that starts with "Can you hear me?" and ends with "Hello?" adds 24 hours to the response time.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU TAKE A PHOTO OF YOUR SCREEN WITH YOUR PHONE...
bullets: A photograph of your monitor taken at a 45-degree angle with potato-quality lighting and visible fingerprints is not a screenshot.
Screenshots exist. There is a button on your keyboard. It says "PrtScn." Use it. If you do not know where it is, ask Google before you ask me.
If you must photograph the screen, hold the phone steady, turn off the flash, and do not include your coffee mug, your lunch, or your reflection in the frame.
Note: A blurry photo of a blurry error message that you immediately closed before I could read it does not help me. At all.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU WHATSAPP ME AT 11 PM 'JUST A QUICK QUESTION'...
bullets: The IT Bible has a verse about this: "Just a quick question is never quick, and it is rarely just a question."
Texting me after hours for a non-emergency does not make you proactive. It makes you the reason I turn off read receipts.
If the office is closed and the building is locked, the password reset can wait until morning. The server is not going anywhere.
Note: My WhatsApp status says "Support hours: 8-5." Your message saying "I know but this is urgent" at 10 PM is a violation of the digital social contract.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU SEND A WALL OF 20 SCREENSHOTS WITH NO CONTEXT...
bullets: Twenty screenshots of different error messages from different applications with no explanation is not a support ticket. It is a digital ransom note.
Circle the relevant part. Number them. Tell me what order to look at them. I am a technician, not a detective reconstructing your workflow from disjointed visual evidence.
"See attached" with 47 files named "Screenshot(1).png" through "Screenshot(47).png" is how you get ignored until you provide actual context.
Note: Screenshots are evidence. Context is the investigation. Provide both or expect no conviction.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU ASK ME TO 'JUST FIX IT VIA WHATSAPP'...
bullets: I cannot reboot your server from my phone's WhatsApp interface. I cannot remote into your machine via text message. I cannot deploy a patch through an image attachment.
Remote support requires a remote support tool. That requires you to be at your computer. That requires you to have scheduled a session.
"Can't you just do your IT magic from there?" — no. My "IT magic" requires a VPN connection, your cooperation, and you not walking away mid-session.
Note: WhatsApp is for quick coordination, not full-scale infrastructure repairs. Call me old-fashioned, but some things require an actual computer.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU SEND ME A SCREENSHOT OF A SCREENSHOT...
bullets: A screenshot of a screenshot that has been compressed, forwarded three times, and received as a low-resolution JPEG is illegible.
The error message text has been reduced to indistinguishable pixels. The QR code cannot be scanned. The serial number has become abstract art.
The original screenshot was clear. Why did you not send that one? Why did you take a screenshot of the screenshot and then send the meta-screenshot?
Note: Screenshot-ception is not impressive. It is infuriating. Send the original or do not bother.

warnings.title: BEFORE YOU SEND A 'VOICE NOTE' EXPLAINING THE PROBLEM...
bullets: A voice note longer than 5 minutes about a printer issue is not acceptable in any universe.
You could have typed the entire problem in 30 seconds. You chose to record a 4-minute rambling monologue with three interruptions, background TV noise, and heavy breathing into the microphone.
I will transcribe it. Badly. Then I will respond with a single sentence because that is all the actual issue required.
